 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Chris Eubanks was surprised that Flavio Cobolli went down without much of a fight in his ATP Finals defeat to Frances Tiafoe. 
 The former player did, however, admit that his fellow American Tiafoe deserves plenty of credit for creating that scenario. He defeated home favourite Cobolli 7-6(8-6), 6-0 in their round-robin match. It represents a maiden ATP Finals victory for Tiafoe, who like Cobolli is making his debut at the year-end tournament in Turin, Italy.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The American now meets Daniil Medvedev for a place in the semifinals, while the Italian cannot qualify after back-to-back losses. The one-hour, 30-minute match at the Inalpi Arena has now been discussed by Eubanks and Mark Petchey.
 Chris Eubanks surprised by Flavio Cobolli's attitude vs Frances Tiafoe
 Breaking down the match on Tennis Channel , former ATP player Sam Querrey asked Eubanks and Petchey the question: "Were you guys surprised by Cobolli? It's his first time at the year-end finals, it's in Italy. He loses a close first set. He completely goes away in the second set. Were you surprised that he wasn't able to dig down and at least make that second set somewhat of a fight?"
 Eubanks replied: "Yeah, I was. Especially in front of a home crowd and quick conditions. We talked a lot about Cobolli's serve and the first serve percentage being pretty low, but on quick courts he has the ability to put a 130 into the box.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "You would have thought he would have at least been able to get a hold, just try to give the crowd something to kind of jump behind. There was none of that, and I think a lot of credit though has to go to Frances. We can talk about Cobolli kind of losing the energy, feeling dejected.
 "Frances forced that feeling from Cobolli to continue because of how well he was playing, how solid he was playing. So while yes it was a bit surprising for Cobolli, I've got to give Frances a lot of credit for kind of forcing that, putting his foot down and not letting up."
 Petchey added: "Yeah and we talked yesterday obviously about matchups in tennis in terms of Ben [Shelton] and Sascha [Zverev], and it's not been a good one for Ben. You can actually see in the second set, this is never going to be a great matchup I don't feel for Cobolli against Frances.
 "There's just more on the ball, there's better depth consistently from him. You always feel as though he's reacting to what Frances is doing, rather than being able to impose himself. And the best players in the world, as much as they get strategy, 95% of their wins come because they're simply better than the opponent down the other end."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Frances Tiafoe impresses Chris Eubanks at the ATP Finals
 The two analysts had discussed a different area of the clash shortly before, with Petchey having commented: "There was a very noticeable difference in terms of firepower off the ground."
 Agreeing, Eubanks said: "Yeah, very much so. I felt like Cobolli was the one just… felt like he was so juiced up. Obviously this is a big event for him, playing in front of a home crowd, first time. He's going to want to get the win, and he came out firing. I think Frances gifted him some errors to start the match, four unforced errors to get broken. Wins the first eight points does Cobolli and then Frances just turns the tide.
 "The thing I was most impressed with though, he was so solid in defending from both sides, both the forehand, but especially the backhand. I love Frances' backhand. It's so compact. It works really well on quick courts and quick conditions, and especially 6-4 in that breaker he had to scrap out a few backhands out of the corner. Didn't try to do too much, stayed disciplined, stayed solid, was able to claw his way back into that breaker and just ran away with the second."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement While there was major disappointment for Cobolli, who was tearful after the defeat on home soil, Tiafoe must now turn his focus to another huge match. And if their history is anything to go by, he goes into that clash with Medvedev as the underdog, having won just two of their eight career meetings so far.
